title: Recycling solid waste into manufacturing feedstock
bottleneck: A Mars crew generates tons of solid waste — packaging, food waste, hygiene products, eventually worn-out equipment — and discarding mass is unaffordable when every kilogram was launched across interplanetary space. Converting waste into 3D-printer filament, compost, or construction material requires processing plants handling heterogeneous, sometimes hazardous inputs reliably for years. The ISS simply bags trash for destructive reentry; a Mars base has no 'away' to throw things to.
why_it_blocks: Waste is stranded mass and a hygiene hazard; closing the solid-waste loop is required for the same reason as water and air — without it, resupply mass never drops to sustainable levels.
current_state: The ISS demonstrates trash compaction; NASA's waste-conversion projects study the chemistry at small scale. No operational waste-to-feedstock system has flown.
